description: The five planner scenarios from SPEC.md section 8.9. Expected outcomes follow the SPEC table and Appendix C.

requests.intent: A 4 x 3 x 1 factorial in triplicate that fits as asked. Anything other than exactly this design is unfaithful.
requests.arithmetic: 12 conditions x 3 + 4 controls = 40 wells. Catalyst 278 of 1080 uL usable (SPEC Appendix C).

requests.intent: 120 sample wells against 92. A faithful repair keeps to the requested values, keeps co-solvent at 20%, and keeps at least half of the requested sample wells. Cutting to duplicate (80 sample wells) or dropping some conditions are both fine.
requests.arithmetic: 40 conditions x 3 = 120 sample wells against 92. In duplicate: 80 + 4 controls = 84 wells, catalyst 888 uL (SPEC Appendix C).

requests.intent: 15 mol % and 3.5 equiv are outside the allowed ranges (max 10 and 3.0). Drop them or clamp them to 10 and 3.0, and declare it. The in-range values 5 and 10 mol % and 1.5 equiv must stay, whether the out-of-range values are dropped or clamped, as must four replicates and 10% co-solvent.
requests.arithmetic: Dropping both: 2 conditions x 4 = 8 sample wells. Clamping both: 4 conditions x 4 = 16 sample wells. Either fits easily.

requests.intent: No numbers given. The usual conditions are the reference control (2.0 mol %, 1.5 equiv, 20%). A faithful design includes those usual values (2.0 mol % catalyst, 1.5 equiv base, 20% co-solvent each appear somewhere), at least one base level above 1.5, and lists what it assumed.
requests.arithmetic: Any small screen fits. The check is on the content, not the size.

requests.intent: Catalyst at 10 mol % everywhere is the point of the request, so a repair must keep it and cut wells instead. Lowering the catalyst to save reagent is unfaithful. Base and co-solvent values must come from the request.
requests.arithmetic: 33 conditions x 3 = 99 sample wells against 92. In duplicate, 66 sample wells use 1320 uL of catalyst plus 8 uL for the reference controls = 1328 uL against 1080 usable (SPEC Appendix C). At 20 uL per well, at most 53 sample wells fit.
